graphStyle.title: Style
graphStyle.button.label: Style ({count} rules)
graphStyle.forGraphData: Rules for graph data: in the graph panel, for the graph on the map and in node and edge tables made from a graph.
graphStyle.order: Rules apply from top to bottom. When two rules set the same target for the same node, the lower one wins. {keys} change the order.
graphStyle.kind.label: Rules for
graphStyle.empty.title: No rules yet
graphStyle.empty.nodes: Color, size and shape come from the basis. With a rule you highlight what matters to you.
graphStyle.empty.edges: Edges are drawn by the panel options. With a rule you highlight edges by type or property.
graphStyle.copy.label: Take over rules from another panel
graphStyle.copy.hint: Replaces the rules of this panel with a copy. Nothing is linked: when the other panel changes, this one stays as it is.
graphStyle.copy.confirm: The {count} rules of this panel are replaced by the rules of “{title}”.
graphStyle.newer: These rules come from a newer version of Kalzit. They are drawn as far as this version can read them and stay stored unchanged; they cannot be changed here.
graphStyle.target.label: Label
graphStyle.state.dormant: resting: “{property}” does not occur in the result
graphStyle.state.invalid: resting: the value does not fit the data type
graphStyle.form.label: Applies to nodes with label
graphStyle.form.dateHint: A day such as 2022-01-01 or a point in time such as 2022-01-01T08:30:00Z.
graphStyle.form.listHint: Lists and nested values: only “exists” and “contains” (an element of the list).
graphStyle.form.colorPerValue: Each value gets a color from the data palette.
graphStyle.form.labelHint: Text or {example} for the value of a property.
graphStyle.form.secondCue: Good, warning and critical state something. Add a second cue (badge, shape or icon) so the meaning does not rest on color alone.
graphStyle.error.number: “{property}” is a number. Enter a number, for example 10000.
graphStyle.error.days: Enter a number of days, for example 30.
graphStyle.values.hint: The palette has eight colors; from the ninth value on it repeats with another shape, from the thirteenth the rest falls under “Other”. A value keeps its color when the result changes.
graphStyle.legend.title: Rules
graphStyle.sheet.label: Panel style
graphStyle.sheet.viewOnly: Changes here apply only for you and only in this view. They are saved in edit mode.
graphStyle.table.hint: For node and edge tables made from a graph: color as a dot before the value, icon and badge at the label, a label rule replaces the text. An edge table takes only the color. The table needs the column @labels or @type for it.
graphStyle.table.ruleWins: Column {column}: rule {rule} applies before the color scheme, thresholds and value mappings of this column. They stay saved and apply again when the rule is off.
